authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 102 — Subject matter of copyright
authorities_checked.proposition: Copyright subsists in original works fixed in a tangible medium; musical works and sound recordings are listed categories; ideas are excluded.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 106 — Exclusive rights
authorities_checked.proposition: Lists exclusive rights subject to statutory limitations; the sound-recording public-performance right is § 106(6), for digital audio transmission.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 114 — Scope of sound-recording rights
authorities_checked.proposition: Sound-recording rights are limited by statute; § 114(b) distinguishes recapture of actual recorded sounds from independently fixed sounds that imitate them.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 101 — Definitions
authorities_checked.pinpoint: Definitions of “joint work” and “work made for hire”
authorities_checked.proposition: Defines a joint work through authorship and intent to merge contributions; gives two work-made-for-hire routes and a limited list for specially ordered/commissioned works.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 201 — Ownership of copyright
authorities_checked.proposition: Initial ownership vests in author(s); joint-work authors are coowners; a work made for hire treats employer/commissioning party as author subject to written contrary agreement.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 204 — Execution of transfers
authorities_checked.proposition: A transfer of copyright ownership other than by operation of law requires a writing signed by the owner or duly authorized agent.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 408 — Registration in general
authorities_checked.proposition: Registration is not a condition of copyright protection.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 411 — Registration and civil actions
authorities_checked.proposition: Sets a registration/preregistration requirement before civil infringement action for U.S. works, with statutory exceptions and a refusal-of-registration procedure.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 412 — Registration and certain remedies
authorities_checked.proposition: Limits statutory damages and attorney-fee awards for specified pre-registration infringements, subject to exceptions including qualifying preregistration and a three-month post-publication path.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 115 — Mechanical licensing
authorities_checked.proposition: Provides conditional licensing routes for reproduction/distribution of nondramatic musical works, including a blanket license for eligible digital music providers and covered activities.

authorities_checked.title: 17 U.S.C. § 107 — Fair use
authorities_checked.proposition: Lists illustrative fair-use purposes and four nonexclusive factors for case-specific evaluation.

authorities_checked.title: U.S. Copyright Office Circular 30, Works Made for Hire (rev. Aug. 2024)
authorities_checked.proposition: Explains the two statutory work-made-for-hire routes, commissioned categories, signed written agreement requirement, and that status depends on facts existing when work was created.
